narrative.setting: Broward County is a large metropolitan county in the Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach area with 2,013,317 residents in 2025, among the most populous counties in the country. Its employment base and infrastructure stand well above the national norm, while migration and natural hazard exposure weigh against it.
narrative.moving: Covered employment reached 863,595 in 2025, up 12.6 percent over five years, among the faster-growing job bases nationally, which supports office, retail and housing demand. Unemployment averaged 3.7 percent after a 5.6-point decline, one of the sharpest improvements in the country. Commercial parcels carry $51.6B in assessed value, $25,637 per resident, well above the national norm. Substations reach 500 kV and 150.5 miles of high-voltage transmission run through the county, alongside 170.8 interstate miles.
narrative.favors: Dense interstate coverage with six interstate junctions favors warehouse and industrial projects. High-voltage transmission makes power-intensive uses such as data centers plausible. The commercial value base and median household income of $77,633, up 27.4 percent in five years, support commercial lending and retail now.
narrative.watch: Net domestic migration was -29,517 in 2025, among the weakest in the nation, and has worsened over five years, a drag on housing absorption. Tax-return flows show a net loss of 656.4 people per 100,000 residents in 2023. Natural hazard risk is far higher than in most counties, with expected annual losses of $648.0M, raising insurance and underwriting costs.
narrative.provide: Red Planet Data already holds parcel, owner entity, sales, deed, mortgage and loan, lien, court filing, foreclosure and tax sale auction, building permit, zoning, code enforcement and government meeting records, and can provide them in under a day. Tax status records are not available because the county does not offer them in a form that can be collected.
